newsitem.title: LATVIA: LAT FIRM VS DOLLAR, INVESTOR INFLOWS EXPECTED.
newsitem.headline: LAT FIRM VS DOLLAR, INVESTOR INFLOWS EXPECTED.

text.p: The lat firmed slightly against the dollar on Tuesday after easing late last week but dealers said there were no pointers to a major change in the coming days.
The lat was traded at 0.5713/0.5718 to the dollar in the afternoon versus 0.5721/25 on Friday amid slow activity.
"The dollar has gone up against the SDR but eased slightly versus the lat," a dealer said.
About three million dollars had been traded on Latvia's currency market by afternoon, a drop from Monday's nine million and transactions were below the average $500,000, dealers said.
Dealers saw the lat rate against the dollar for now being determined by larger capital inflows into Latvia as investors buy lats to settle privatisation deals.
Russian gas giant Gazprom is among those expected soon to have to buy lats as it pays for a 16.25 percent stake in gas supplier Latvian Gas.
"This keeps the rate close to the central bank intervention rate where, in other words, the dollar is cheap and the lat expensive," a dealer told Reuters.
The central bank's intervention rate to the dollar is currently 0.5712 lats, dealers said.
